entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Iytjenu was an ancient Egyptian king of the First Intermediate Period, whose reign is only indirectly attested due to a royal cartouche in the name of Zat-Iytjenu - Daughter of Iytjenu. This cartouche signifies that Zat-Iytjenu's name refers to her father, Iytjenu, indicating he was a king.

The First Intermediate Period followed the Middle Kingdom and preceded the New Kingdom, a time marked by instability and fragmentation in ancient Egypt. Iytjenu's existence during this era underscores the complexities of Egyptian politics during this period.

Iytjenu's legacy is tied to the brief resurgence of centralized authority in Egypt before the eventual decline into further regionalization and foreign intervention.

The discovery of Zat-Iytjenu's name, with its royal cartouche, serves as a poignant reminder that even the most fragmented historical records can reveal glimpses of powerful leaders who shaped the course of history.
